questions.evidence:
WALL PLAN: A board has twelve equal spaces. Each selected story uses two spaces, including its title and illustration. A large introduction uses two spaces, and a visitor question card uses one. The remaining spaces may hold stories; no story may be split across boards.

EDITOR'S LIST: Five stories have been selected. Each has between one hundred and one hundred and fifty words. The team wants to display all five on opening day. A second small board has four matching spaces and can stand beside the first board.

PRINTING NOTE: One printed story set costs twenty dollars. The introduction costs fifteen, and the question card costs five. The budget is one hundred and thirty dollars. Borrowing the small board is free, and none of the selected texts needs another illustration.

The team counts usable spaces before printing. They put four stories, the introduction, and the question card on the large board. The fifth story goes on the small board. They keep unused space clear instead of enlarging a story without its writer's agreement.
